e-9520.knowledge_point: Writing a Factorial in an Equivalent Form
e-9520.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to $(k+1)!$ for any $k \geq 2?$

- $(k+1) \cdot k \cdot (k-1)$

- $(k+1) \cdot k \cdot (k-1)!$

- $(k+1) \cdot k$
e-9520.worked_solution:
Using the definition of factorial, we have 

$$
(k+1)! = (k+1) \cdot k \cdot (k-1) \cdot (k-2) \cdot \: \cdots \: \cdot 2 \cdot 1.
$$

Now, applying the factorial definition to all but the first two factors, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(k+1)! & =(k+1)\cdot k\cdot \overset{(k-1)!}{\overset{⏞}{(k-1)\cdot (k-2)\cdot \,⋯\,\cdot 2\cdot 1}} \\  & =(k+1)\cdot k\cdot (k-1)!\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

e-5669.knowledge_point: Simplifying a Variable Expression Containing a Quotient of Factorials
e-5669.problem: Given that $n \geq 2$ is an integer, simplify $\dfrac {n!} {(n - 2)!}.$
e-5669.worked_solution:
First, notice the following:

$$
n! = n \cdot (n-1) \cdot (n-2)!
$$

Then, we cancel the $(n-2)!$ that occurs in both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\eqalign{
\dfrac {n!} {(n - 2)!} 
&= \dfrac {n \cdot (n - 1) \cdot (n - 2)!} {(n - 2)!}\[5pt] 

&= \dfrac {n \cdot (n - 1) \cdot \cancel{(n - 2)!}} {\cancel{(n - 2)!}}\[5pt] 

&= n(n -1) \[5pt]
&= n^2 - n
	}
$$

e-5670.knowledge_point: Simplifying a Variable Expression Containing a Quotient With Many Factorials
e-5670.problem: Given that $k \geq 1$ is an integer, simplify $\dfrac {k^2(k - 1)!} {k!}.$
e-5670.worked_solution:
First, we notice that 

$$
k! = k \cdot (k-1)!
$$

So, we can simplify the numerator as follows:

$$
k^2 (k-1)! = k \cdot \underbrace{k \cdot (k-1)!}_{k!} = k \cdot k!
$$

Then, we cancel the $k!$ that occurs in both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\eqalign{
\dfrac {k^2(k - 1)!} {k!} 
&= \dfrac {k \cdot k!} {k!}\[5pt]
&= \dfrac {k \cdot \cancel{k!}} {\cancel{k!}} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac {k} {1} \[5pt]
&= k
	}
$$

after.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $(n+6)!$ for any $n\ge -3?$
after.worked_solution:
Using the definition of factorial, we have

$$
(n+6)!=(n+6)\cdot (n+5)\cdot (n+4)\cdot \,⋯\,\cdot 2\cdot 1.
$$

Now, applying the factorial definition to all but the first factor, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(n+6)! & =(n+6)\cdot \overset{(n+5)!}{\overset{⏞}{(n+5)\cdot (n+4)\cdot \,⋯\,\cdot 2\cdot 1}} \\  & =(n+6)\cdot (n+5)!\end{aligned}
$$

a

decision.explanation: Using m! = m(m-1)!, (n-4)! = (n-4)·(n-5)!, so option a is correct. This also holds at n=5 because 0! = 1.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $(n-4)!$ for any $n\ge 5?$
after.worked_solution:
Using the definition of factorial, we have

$$
(n-4)!=(n-4)\cdot (n-5)\cdot (n-6)\cdot \,⋯\,\cdot 2\cdot 1.
$$

Now, applying the factorial definition to all but the first factor, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(n-4)! & =(n-4)\cdot \overset{(n-5)!}{\overset{⏞}{(n-5)\cdot (n-6)\cdot \,⋯\,\cdot 2\cdot 1}} \\  & =(n-4)\cdot (n-5)!\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem: Given that $n\ge 1$ is an integer, simplify $\frac{(n+1)!}{(n-1)!}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice the following:

$$
(n+1)!=(n+1)\cdot n\cdot (n-1)!
$$

Then, we cancel the $(n-1)!$ that occurs in both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(n+1)!}{(n-1)!} & =\frac{(n+1)\cdot n\cdot (n-1)!}{(n-1)!} \\  & =\frac{(n+1)\cdot n\cdot \cancel{(n-1)!}}{\cancel{(n-1)!}} \\  & =n(n+1)\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: Given that $k\ge 0$ is an integer, simplify $\frac{(k+3)!}{(k+1)k!}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice the following:

$$
(k+3)!=(k+3)\cdot (k+2)\cdot (k+1)\cdot k!
$$

Then, we cancel the $k!$ and $(k+1)$ that occurs in both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(k+3)!}{(k+1)k!}= & \frac{(k+3)\cdot (k+2)\cdot (k+1)\cdot k!}{(k+1)\cdot k!} \\ = & \frac{(k+3)\cdot (k+2)\cdot \cancel{(k+1)}\cdot \cancel{k!}}{\cancel{(k+1)}\cdot \cancel{k!}} \\ = & (k+3)(k+2) \\ = & {k}^{2}+5k+6\,.\end{aligned}

content.knowledge_point: Simplifying a Variable Expression Containing a Quotient of Factorials
content.problem: Given that $k\ge 0$ is an integer, simplify $\frac{(k+3)!}{(k+1)k!}.$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice the following:

$$
(k+3)!=(k+3)\cdot (k+2)\cdot (k+1)\cdot k!
$$

Then, we cancel the $k!$ and $(k+1)$ that occurs in both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(k+3)!}{(k+1)k!}= & \frac{(k+3)\cdot (k+2)\cdot (k+1)\cdot k!}{(k+1)\cdot k!} \\ = & \frac{(k+3)\cdot (k+2)\cdot \cancel{(k+1)}\cdot \cancel{k!}}{\cancel{(k+1)}\cdot \cancel{k!}} \\ = & (k+3)(k+2) \\ = & {k}^{2}+5k+6\,.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 9
after.problem: Given that $k\ge 0$ is an integer, simplify $\frac{(k+1)!}{k!}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice the following:

$$
(k+1)!=(k+1)\cdot k!
$$

Then, we cancel the $k!$ that occurs in both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(k+1)!}{k!} & =\frac{(k+1)\cdot k!}{k!} \\  & =\frac{(k+1)\cdot \cancel{k!}}{\cancel{k!}} \\  & =k+1\end{aligned}
$$
